messages:
zephyr-ops: Hey team — our production service (zephyr-prod) started seeing a flurry of 429s at ~16:10 PDT. Requests to /v1/generate are getting throttled, clients see 'rate_limited' and token-per-second SLOs are breached. We're on Dedicated pool zephyr-prod-pool. Can you check?

sophie: Sorry you're hitting this — I'm looking. Can you paste a sample request id and the time window? Any recent traffic pattern changes? :eyes:

zephyr-ops: Sample req id: req_0a9f3c. Spike was sudden — a partner batch job emitted a burst around 16:09-16:12, ~18k TPS for 30s then back down. No config changes on our side.

omar: Got it — pinging runtime. Do we have admission logs for that pool? early sign is burst credits drained then admission controller started rejecting.

admission-bot: [admission-event] pool=zephyr-prod-pool time=2026-03-12T23:09:48Z event=burst_credit_consumed tenant=zephyr amt=32000 remaining=0
admission-bot: [admission-event] pool=zephyr-prod-pool time=2026-03-12T23:09:49Z event=admit_reject tenant=zephyr reason=no_headroom code=429

lee: Admission shows credits exhausted then immediate rejects — but race looks odd: autoscaler appears to be launching extra slots but they come online ~22s after rejection spike. That delay explains SLO misses.

tess: The customer is asking why Dedicated autoscale didn't prevent 429s. They want mitigation and a short-term workaround.

sophie: Immediate actions: 1) Ask Zephyr to toggle burst backfill (if available) or temporarily increase pool burst_quota. 2) We'll investigate autoscale cold start lag and consider prewarm.

omar: Notes from infra: logs show GPU scheduling churn and slot init time ~= 18-25s during that window. Example snippet: ```
[23:09:48.102] slot-init start slot=slot-7a3
[23:09:55.340] slot-ready slot=slot-7a3 host=gpu-12
[23:09:55.342] slot-register pool=zephyr-prod-pool
```

lee: Also spotted noisy neighbor behavior: another tenant on same host (tenant=lodestar) spiked KV-cache pressure and consumed 3/4 of pool ephemeral headroom. Admission logs: ```
[23:09:47] admit_check tenant=lodestar used_headroom=0.75 total_headroom=1.0
[23:09:48] admit_check tenant=zephyr used_headroom=1.0 total_headroom=1.0 -> reject
```

zephyr-ops: Is there anything we can do right now besides raising burst_quota? We can't change partner job.

omar: Short-term options: - Increase pool burst_quota (requires ops intervention) - Move zephyr-prod to a dedicated reserved pool (isolate noisy neighbors) - Temporarily route critical traffic to hosted API fallback (if acceptable)

lee: Also recommend tuning admission controller to prefer fairness by tenant when headroom < 20% (will lower single-tenant 429s during noisy spikes). That's a code change and needs off-hours rollout.

sophie: Repro steps for eng if you want to simulate: 1) Use load generator to send a 30s burst at 18k TPS to /v1/generate with same token sizes. 2) Observe admission-bot events and slot boot latency. Example curl (load generator snippet): ```bash
for i in $(seq 1 18000); do curl -s -X POST https://zephyr.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"x"}' & done
```

omar: Added a ticket to SRE queue: "zephyr-prod autoscale cold-start latency and admission fairness". Assigning to @lee. Ticket id: SRE-2026-812.

lee: Plan: 1) Investigate slot init path and prewarm heuristics (today) 2) Add temporary per-pool burst_quota bump for Zephyr (with billing ops ok) (next 30m) 3) Longer term: admission fairness change + host isolation recommendation for high-SLO customers.

sophie: I've authorized temporary burst_quota bump + notified billing for charge approval. Zephyr — can you confirm if 429s stop in the next 10m?

zephyr-ops: Seeing retries clear-out around 16:25 PDT, 429s dropped to baseline. Will monitor and report if anything else. Thanks folks. :heart:

admission-bot: [note] manual_quota_change pool=zephyr-prod-pool burst_quota=+50% initiated_by=sophie time=2026-03-12T23:16:05Z

sophie: Closing loop: created postmortem checklist items (prewarm improvements, per-tenant headroom metrics, ops playbook for rapid quota bump). Marking thread for follow-up with product and SRE.
